Independent analytical replay from Schur products of adjacency projectors and termwise finite Cesàro limits
correctness.rationale: Replayed via the star's adjacency spectral projectors E_0,E_+,E_- at 0,+nu,-nu. E_0 is the leaf-contrast projector. E_± have hub-hub entry 1/2, hub-leaf entry ±1/(2 sqrt(r)), and leaf-leaf entry 1/(2r). In the instantaneous mixing matrix the per-sign Fourier coefficients F_{±1}=E_0∘(E_++E_-) equal Q_L/r. F_{±2}=E_+∘E_- is (r+1)Q_R/(4r) by its radial row and zero row sums. The zero mode follows from M(0)=I: eigenvalues 1,(r-2)/r,(r-1)/(2r). Thus the stated polynomials and orthogonal sectors apply at every t. The commuting Cartesian summands give a tensor product before Cesàro averaging, and each finite Fourier term survives exactly when its weighted frequency is zero. All surviving weights in each sector are nonnegative; the resulting dimensions and kernel description follow without cancellations. All local constants are positive for r>=3, while an isolated contrast in any r=2 factor stays null at all weights. Off the bounded relation hyperplanes only zero modes survive, yielding the generic rank. Equal-frequency P3 powers allow exactly an even number of contrast factors, giving (3^d+1)/2; in P3 times K_{1,3}, the two distinct positive-frequency ratios restore dimensions two and one respectively, giving ranks 10 and 9 over the baseline 8.
residual_risks: Strictly positive couplings, finite products, exact real resonances, no interaction terms. Tensorization is for the instantaneous matrix, not the average at one shared clock.

evidence: General projector expressions and bounds, an exact algorithm for unweighted graphs, and a trace/covariance identity for synchronous Cartesian products are available.

evidence: For a product, the all-zero Fourier term is the tensor product of the single-factor averages; all other surviving terms are tensor products of Schur products of positive semidefinite projectors. Thus positive single-factor averages imply positive definiteness of the product. A lone P3 null vector tensored with constant vectors stays null, since the other instantaneous matrices fix their constants.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This credits positivity as a short consequence once one-factor ranks are known. The checked sources do not give the full pattern of kernel restoration at resonances. Extracting the radial Fourier block and comparing it to the leaf block is what permits the complete exact classification rather than just the positivity boundary.

originality.rationale: Pass applies to the explicit three-sector weighted star-product spectrum and resonance rank/kernel classification. The general projector formula, synchronous tensorization and signed-frequency technique are established. Prior one-star work and the general projector identity already provide a short route to the robust positivity criterion alone; it is a consequence here, not the distinguishing advance. The extra radial sector and ±2 effective-frequency modes create rank jumps not covered by the inspected precedents.
residual_risks: Possible unpublished or unlocated general Fourier-sector theorem or overlapping thesis material is not ruled out; the result is not credited with novelty for the shared-clock framework or one-star rank.

value.rationale: Stars are a natural class containing a singular one-factor average (P3) and positive ones. For coupled clock frequencies the exact kernel can shrink without disappearing, and different commensurabilities restore different dimensions, even in the smallest hybrid. The sector calculation separates that phenomenon from known factor positivity and supplies a reusable exact rank and nullspace test instead of re-diagonalizing each product Hamiltonian.
residual_risks: Exact rank is discontinuous on some resonant strata; the result does not quantify finite-window robustness or mixing time.
